knowledge_point.title: Using the Double-Angle Formula to Simplify Ratios

question.:question/worked-solution:
Write $s=\sin\left(70^\circ\right)$ and $c=\cos\left(70^\circ\right)$. The **double-angle formula** gives $\sin\left(140^\circ\right)=2sc$.

 Also, $\cot\left(70^\circ\right)=\frac{c}{s}$.

Rewrite the quotient ratio and use $s^2+c^2=1$ to obtain a difference of squares. Factor before cancelling.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{2sc\frac{c}{s}-1}{c+s} &=\frac{2c^2-1}{c+s} \\ &=\frac{c^2-s^2}{c+s} \\ &=\frac{(c-s)(c+s)}{c+s} \\ &=c-s \\ &=\cos\left(70^\circ\right)-\sin\left(70^\circ\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

All cancellations use nonzero factors in the original expression.

generation.domain: Original denominators and reciprocal functions must be defined; sampled angles are acute and nonspecial.

question.:question/worked-solution:
Write $s=\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{20}\right)$ and $c=\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{20}\right)$. The **double-angle formula** gives $\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{10}\right)=2sc$.

 Also, $\tan\left(\frac{\pi}{20}\right)=\frac{s}{c}$.

Rewrite the quotient ratio and cancel. Use $s^2+c^2=1$, factor the difference of squares, then cancel the matching binomial.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{2sc\frac{s}{c}}{(1+c)} &=\frac{2s^2}{(1+c)} \\ &=2\frac{1-c^2}{(1+c)} \\ &=2\frac{(1-c)(1+c)}{(1+c)} \\ &=2(1-c) \\ &=2\left(1-\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{20}\right)\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

All cancellations use nonzero factors in the original expression.
